ACR of Judicial Officers 16
Guidelines for Reporting Officer/ Authority
1. In awarding marks against each item in the ACR, preferably
brief reasoning is to be given in the ‘Remark’ column against
each item of Group-A, Group-B, Group-C and Group-D.
Assessment regarding items under Group-A
In respect of awarding marks against item no. (a), (b), (c) and
(d), the Registrar (Vigilance), High Court of Meghalaya shall
remain vigilant and assist the Reporting Authority concerned
during the year of assessment to ascertain the concerned
Judicial Officer’s punctuality, control over Court proceedings,
relationship with the Bar and administrative control.
Assessment regarding items under Group-B
2. In this respect, the Reporting Officer/Authority, apart from
evaluating the judgments submitted by the Judicial Officer
concerned shall have the liberty to make his assessment on
the basis of judgment(s)/ order(s) which have been
challenged in his Court on appellate/ revisional side or
otherwise, and in that case, the Reporting Officer/Authority
has to enclose the copy(ies) of the said judgment(s)/ order(s)
with the ACR of Judicial Officer concerned.
Assessment regarding items under Group-C
3. In awarding marks under this group, the Reporting
Officer/Authority shall have due regards in disposal of old
pending cases in case of Judicial Officers posted in Court. In
case of ‘Outstanding’ grading in overall disposal, the marks
will be awarded within a range of 80% to 100% of total marks
(70) e.g. if the Officer has disposed of large number of old
cases i.e. 5 years or more against the pendency at the
beginning of the year, he/she may be awarded 100% marks
and similarly, if any Judicial Officer, though has obtained
outstanding marks, has disposed only negligible number of
such old pending cases or no old pending cases despite such
cases being pending in his/her Court, the maximum mark
which can be awarded is 80% out of total 70 marks. In this
ACR of Judicial Officers 17
way, the marks of Judicial Officers scoring ‘outstanding’, ‘very
good’, ‘good’, ‘average’ and ‘poor’ in disposal of cases will
respectively be awarded within the following range:

based on the performance in the fields of Legal Services
work, administrative work, mediation and disposal of cases

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS
a. Page nos. 1-12 shall be filled up by the Judicial Officer
concerned/Assessed Officer; Page nos. 13-14 shall be filled up by the
Judicial officer/Assessed Officer attached to the Legal Services Authorities;
Page nos. 18-21 shall be filled by the Reporting Officer/Authority; Page
No. 22 shall be filled up by the Registrar (Vigilance), Page No. 23 shall be
filled up by the Accepting Authority.
b. ACRs of Grade I Judicial Officers shall be submitted directly to the
Registrar (Vigilance), High Court of Meghalaya.
c. With regard to the ACRs of Judicial Officers attached to the Legal
Services Authorities, the Reporting Authority shall make a grading of
the Judicial Officer on the basis of FORM B, general assessment of the
officer and his/her integrity.
d. If a Judicial Officer works in different stations/ Courts for the reporting
period, the Reporting Officer/Authority will be the
Portfolio/Administrative Judge under whom he/she is presently working
or under whom he/she worked for more than 3 (three) months.
e. If a Judicial Officer fails to furnish true information, the same will be
viewed very seriously even entailing disciplinary proceedings.
f. The following timelines shall be followed for submission of ACRs of
